heuristic.applicability: Use only when drawer_position is near open and stable, the gripper is initially open or the block is already plausibly held, object_pose is finite and reliable, and the translated object-relative targets remain collision-free and reachable. It covers approach/alignment, closing, low horizontal extraction, clearance lift, and the beginning of transfer. The object must still occupy a physically valid tunnel pose; translation invariance does not move the tunnel or robot.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer is open near 0.300 and stable; gripper is open and free of the handle; block is low in the tunnel; object pose is reliable; arm is retreating from the drawer or approaching the tunnel.
handoff.exit_conditions: Closed fingers remain near the block, object and TCP move together, block is outside the tunnel and above 0.16 m, and transfer toward the open drawer has started.
handoff.failure_signatures: Object fails to follow TCP after closure, fingers remain open, object remains near the tunnel floor, lateral transfer starts before clearance, IK reports persistent nonconvergence/limit contacts, or object pose becomes unreliable.
handoff.overlap_role: Train all actions 300:840. Actions 300:440 preserve 140 predecessor-overlap actions; actions 680:840 preserve 160 successor-overlap actions, including clearance, reorientation and early transfer.
handoff.successor_readiness: Prefer switching to placement once the object/TCP relative transform is stable under closed fingers, object z is above 0.16 m, and motion has turned toward target_pose; 680:840 supplies action-supervised readiness overlap.

heuristic.limitations: Object-frame equivariance does not guarantee IK reachability, wall clearance, or invariance to tunnel/drawer displacement; the measured joints and world/object features are retained for those dependencies. It is sensitive to object-pose noise and can follow a moving/dropped block reference. It has no contact truth and successful demonstrations do not establish failed-grasp recovery. When the object is near demonstrated support but predecessor TCP/configuration is the main variation, use the current-TCP delta prior; when premature transfer under the tunnel roof is the main concern, use the clearance-guarded destination-frame prior.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Inputs are two causal frames of measured joints/velocities, drawer state, object pose, TCP pose, destination target_pose, object/TCP and destination/object transforms, and tunnel-clearance features. Learned actions are 10-D: object-frame TCP translation in metres, object-frame TCP rotation as the first two rotation-matrix columns, and the native-sign gripper scalar. encode_targets uses FK poses of native commands and each slot's pre-action object pose; decode_action composes the learned pose with the freshly observed object pose and invokes the verified IK from freshly measured joints. Standard DiffusionBackbone and fixed H2/16/8 timing are retained.
heuristic.rationale: The observed initial block positions differ (for example demo12100 is about (-0.4368,-0.4063,0.0800) at 300 and demo12101 is about (-0.4478,-0.4076,0.0800)), while their approach and grasp commands move with the block: at 540 the commanded TCP is about (-0.4367,-0.4019,0.0889) in demo12100 and (-0.4480,-0.4032,0.0888) in demo12101. The demonstrations then pull in -x at low height (600), lift above clearance (640:700), reorient (780), and transfer (820:840). Encoding each demonstrated command in the contemporaneously observed object frame makes approach, alignment, pull, and held-object lift/transfer feedback equivariant to a changed observed object pose by construction. Two-frame object/TCP relations plus measured joints retain phase, reachability, and robot configuration. This is an expected generalization benefit, not evidence for shifts outside the observed range.
heuristic.statement: Object-frame Cartesian target prior: diffuse commanded TCP poses as object-relative SE(3) targets (3-D translation, 6-D rotation, gripper) and resolve the observed block pose again at every executed slot. Prefer this policy when the block is displaced from demonstrated x/y but remains in the tunnel, its pose is reliable, the drawer is open, and the target is reachable.

subgoal: With the drawer already open, move from the drawer-retreat state to the tunnel, descend within the tunnel clearance, align an open gripper around the block, close on it, pull it horizontally out of the tunnel, then lift it above the 0.16 m tunnel clearance and begin transfer toward the drawer. Approximate entry: drawer open and stable, block low near z=0.08, gripper open. Approximate exit: block held with closed fingers and elevated around z=0.30-0.32 or higher, outside the tunnel and moving toward the drawer.
